newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- CREST TARIFFS RISE TO DETER USERS

Crest, the computerised share settlement system, will be raising its tariffs by an average of 15 per cent to provide an extra 3 million pounds stg of revenue. Despite the increase, Iain Saville, Crest's chief executive, concedes that the service will not be sufficient to meet peak demand, even with an increased computer capacity. Mr Saville admits that the increase in tariffs is partly intended to deter City firms from using the system.
-- ABBEY MAY LIFT STAKES IN BID FOR SCOTAM

Abbey National may raise its offer for Scottish Amicable from 1.1 to 1.4 billion pounds stg ready for a takeover battle with Prudential. Charles Toner, deputy chief executive of Abbey National, said yesterday that Prudential's current proposal does not necessarily give any more value than Abbey's own bid. Scottish Amicable delayed its two stage flotation plans on Wednesday while it looks at Prudential's offer which values the company at 1.9 billion pounds stg.
-- VIRTUALITY RUNS INTO REAL PROBLEMS

Virtuality, the best known company in the virtual reality sector, asked for its shares to be suspended yesterday, pending clarification of the group's financial position. Administration or receivership is thought to be only weeks away, unless the company can negotiate a cash injection or a takeover. Philips Electronics, which has a stake of less than 3 per cent in the group was being tipped as a potential buyer last night.
THE TIMES
-- PRU THREATENS DTI WITH LEGAL ACTION OVER 'ORPHANS'

Prudential Corporation is threatening to take legal action against the Department of Trade and Industry because of delays in establishing ownership of 3 billion pounds stg of its orphan assets. The group chief executive, Sir Peter Davis, is thought to be losing patience with the DTI inquiry into surplus assets which began nearly a year ago. If Prudential were to secure a large part of orphan assets, it could clear the way for other life companies to do the same, returning millions of pounds stg to shareholders' funds.
-- STERLING THREAT TO INDUSTRIAL RECOVERY

The pounds strength could undermine the slow recovery in the manufacturing sector. Manufacturing output grew only modestly in December according to new data from the Office of National Statistics. Economist believe that the data supported Kenneth Clarke's decision not to raise interest rates despite pressure from the Bank of England for an increase.
-- STRONG POUND WEIGHS ON ICI

ICI said yesterday that the strong pound could cut its profits by 90 million pounds stg this year and warned that Europe must be competitive with the United States. The chemicals company reported a sharp fall in pre-tax profits, largely caused by a cyclic fall in the price of industrial chemicals. Profits were cut by 15 million pounds stg in the final quarter by the strength of sterling.
THE GUARDIAN
-- EU CHIEF HERALDS FUDGE-FREE EURO

The European Union monetary affairs commissioner said yesterday that delaying monetary union would threaten to bring turmoil to the financial markets and undermining efforts to bring more countries into the community. Mr Yves-Thibault de Silguy believes that union can be carried through only on the basis of sustainable economic convergence and adherence to the terms laid down in the Maastricht treaty. He said there will be no fudging of the criteria, no cooking of the books.
-- SFO DEFEATS THREAT TO COPPER-SCANDAL INQUIRY

The Serious Fraud Office cleared the way for a full resumption of the inquiry into the multi-billion pounds stg copper scandal yesterday, brushing aside an attempt to indict director George Staple for contempt of court. Two High Court judges threw out claims that Mr Staple was in contempt of two injunctions relating to the use of materials seized.
-- HOTEL AND BINGO CALLS HIT BASS

Shares in Bass plunged yesterday following an unexpected profits warning. Chairman, Sir Ian Prosser told the company's annual meeting that business performance in the first quarter of the year was behind expectations. 280 million pounds stg was wiped off the market value of the brewing and leisure group as shares fell 32p to 820.5p.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- GERMAN UNEMPLOYMENT LEAPS TO POST-WAR HIGH

The German headline unemployment figure rose by half-a-million in January, the biggest monthly increase since the early 1930s. The seasonally adjusted figure increased 160,000 from December with the total number of unemployed standing at 4,317 million. Ian Lang, Britain's Trade Secretary jumped on the figures claiming that they showed European social policies were not working and vindicated the Prime Minister's warning to Europe that continental social policies are destroying jobs.
-- BT PROFITS SET TO SOAR AS PENSIONS BURDEN EASES

According to a leading City analyst, British Telecom's profits could rise to 3.4 billion pounds stg next year after the company increased the possibility that the pensions burden caused by its huge voluntary redundancy programme could soon be over. The group had previously had to set aside cash from its earnings to fund future pensions payments, but an actuarial valuation of its pensions liabilities is expected to reveal that the fund was in surplus at the end of last year. James Ross from Hoare Govett, believes the end of this burden will add 200 million pounds stg to BT's annual profits next year.
-- VODAFONE DENIES GERMAN TAKEOVER APPROACH AFTER FRANTIC TRADING

The UK's largest mobile phone operator, Vodafone, made a formal Stock Exchange announcement yesterday, following a frantic period of trading in the company's shares, denying that it had received any takeover approaches. The share price rose 21p in the space of an hour after rumours spread that a German utility giant was preparing to launch a bid. The announcement was made in a bid to calm the markets, but the share price was still up 7p at 285.5p at the close of trading, having at one time reached a record 298p. BMC +44-171-377-1742
